newsitem.title: USA: Cyclones threaten ships in Indian, Pacific Oceans.
newsitem.headline: Cyclones threaten ships in Indian, Pacific Oceans.

text.p: Tropical cyclones are threatening shipping in the Indian Ocean and Southern Pacific, independent forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Monday.
Tropical Cyclone Pancho-Helinda, with 75 mph winds, is nearly stationary in the southern Indian Ocean near 15s/90e.
Tropical Cyclone Iletta, with 60 mph winds, is in the southern Indian Ocean near 16s/71e, moving south-southeast at five mph. It is expected to maintain strength and track slowly southward.
Tropical Cyclone Gretelle, with 50 mph winds, is in the southern Mozambique Channel near 25.8s/38.5e, moving southwest at 6 mph.
Tropical Cyclone Freda is in the southern Pacific, well east of Australia, near 23.4s/176.4e, moving south southeast at 7 mph. Top winds are 65 mph.
